chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ya'qub al-Sarraj and from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said:

When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was given allegiance as the caliph after the killing of Uthman, he ascended the minbar and delivered a speech which he recounted, saying in it: 'Indeed, your affliction has returned to its state as it was when Allah sent His Prophet. And by Him Who sent him with the truth, you will be confused with a great confusion and sifted with a great sifting until your lowest become your highest and your highest become your lowest. And those who were late will hasten, and those who hastened will be delayed. By Allah, I did not hide a sign nor did I tell a lie, and I was inspired with news of this position and this day.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the coming tribulation and social inversion after Uthman's death?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) prophetic foresight of the 'social inversion' and political turbulence that would characterize the era of the Shia, serving as a key hadith for understanding the theological basis for the Occultation. The imagery of 'sifting' (gharbalah) and the reversal of social hierarchies underscores the transition from the clarity of the Prophet’s time to the complex, often obscured, reality of the Imamate's hidden phase. It affirms that the Imamate’s guidance continues amidst chaos, validating the Shia’s endurance through historical trials.
